stem: A client with a newly applied lower-leg cast is preparing for discharge. Which statement indicates correct understanding of home cast care?

options.A: I will keep the cast dry, avoid putting objects inside it, elevate the leg as instructed during the early swelling period, and call promptly for new numbness or inability to move my toes.
options.B: I will keep the cast dry and elevate the leg during the early swelling period, but I can slide a smooth object inside the cast to scratch if the skin is not broken.
options.C: I will keep the cast dry and avoid putting objects inside it, but I can wait until the next routine visit if new numbness develops as long as the pain is manageable.
options.D: I will keep objects out of the cast and report loss of toe movement, but I can soak the cast briefly during bathing if I dry the outside thoroughly afterward.

rationale: AAOS guidance advises keeping a cast dry, avoiding objects inside the cast to scratch, and elevating the injured extremity during the early swelling period. AAOS also directs clients to contact the doctor's office immediately for warning signs such as numbness or tingling and states that loss of active toe or finger movement requires urgent evaluation. Therefore A is correct. B introduces an object under the cast despite the risk of skin irritation or injury. C delays evaluation of a recognized warning sign. D allows cast soaking even though AAOS advises keeping the cast dry and not submerging it unless the treating team has specifically provided waterproof materials and instructions.
educational_objective: Teach safe home cast care by keeping the cast dry, avoiding objects inside the cast, using instructed elevation during early swelling, and promptly reporting neurovascular warning signs such as numbness or loss of toe movement.
source_organization: American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (AAOS), OrthoInfo
source_locator: Getting Used to a Splint or Cast: elevate the injured arm or leg during the early post-injury swelling period to reduce swelling. Warning Signs: contact the doctor's office immediately for increased pain/tightness, numbness/tingling, burning/stinging, excessive distal swelling; loss of active toe/finger movement requires urgent evaluation. Taking Care of Your Splint or Cast: keep the cast dry; do not submerge it; do not insert objects such as coat hangers to scratch itching skin.
source_claim_supported: Safe home cast care includes keeping the cast dry, avoiding inserted objects, elevation during the early swelling period, and prompt evaluation of neurovascular warning signs such as numbness or loss of active toe movement.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort, printed pp. 11 and 35–36: apply, maintain or remove orthopedic devices; implement measures to promote circulation through positioning and mobilization; Mobility/Immobility includes applying knowledge of nursing procedures for clients with immobility and maintaining correct body alignment.
blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — home cast care, positioning, skin protection, and recognition of device-related complications
correction_summary: Rebuilt all four statements to eliminate the very long keyed answer and replace obvious distractors with realistic near-miss home-care errors involving scratching, delayed reporting of numbness, and cast soaking.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Orthopedic care — lower-leg cast home management
audit_findings.stem: PASS — specifies a newly applied lower-leg cast and discharge teaching without requiring an unsupported diagnosis or fixed duration beyond the source's early swelling period.
audit_findings.option_A: PASS — directly combines current AAOS cast-protection, elevation, and warning-sign guidance; uniquely best.
audit_findings.option_B: PASS as distractor — dryness and elevation are appropriate, but inserting an object under the cast conflicts with AAOS skin-protection guidance.
audit_findings.option_C: PASS as distractor — keeping the cast dry and avoiding objects are correct, but new numbness is a warning sign requiring prompt contact rather than routine follow-up.
audit_findings.option_D: PASS as distractor — reporting loss of toe movement is correct, but submerging a standard cast contradicts the instruction to keep it dry.
audit_findings.ambiguity: PASS — A is the only statement without a contradictory cast-care or warning-sign response.
audit_findings.second_answer: EXCLUDED — B inserts an object, C delays a neurovascular warning sign, and D permits cast soaking.
audit_findings.cueing: PASS — all options contain a mix of realistic home-care actions, and the keyed answer is no longer uniquely signaled by extreme wording or markedly greater specificity.
audit_findings.blueprint: PASS — NCSBN Basic Care and Comfort directly includes orthopedic-device care, positioning, circulation-support measures, and mobility/immobility nursing procedures.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — challenged whether a smooth scratching object, delayed numbness follow-up, or brief soaking could be acceptable; current AAOS guidance directly rejects inserted objects and cast submersion and requires prompt contact for numbness, leaving A uniquely correct.
